rounds.text: Metro Brands Ltd is demonstrating robust fundamental compounding, with a 5-year compounded sales growth of 29% [E15] and a 5-year compounded profit growth of 41% [E19], complemented by a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 18% [E21] and sales growth of 14% [E17]. The business generates exceptional operational quality, maintaining a consistent median return on equity of 22% over 1, 3, 5, and 10 years [E24, E25, E26, E27], alongside an impressive return on capital employed of 20.0% [E12] that comfortably outpaces the sector median ROCE of 9.9% [E74]. Cash generation is stellar, evidenced by a cash conversion ratio of 1.19x in March 2026 where profits are fully backed by cash [E32], producing Rs 476 Cr in operating cash flow [E33] and Rs 337 Cr in free cash flow [E34]. Smart institutional capital recognizes these strengths, as foreign and domestic institutions have increased their holdings from 2.33% to 3.73% [E40] and 6.10% to 7.68% [E41] respectively since September 2023, accompanied by positive institutional money flow [E42] and a supportive Consumer Durables sector tailwind score of +0.72 [E69, E71]. Conceded: [E1], [E6], [E43], [E44], [E45], [E68].

While 5-year sales growth of 29% [E15] and 5-year profit growth of 41% [E19] look impressive, the bull ignores severe deceleration where 3-year profit growth has collapsed to 5% [E20] and the rules-based screen explicitly flags earnings growth as decelerating [E65]. Conceded: [E24, E25, E26, E27]. The high return on equity of 22% [E12] and cash generation metrics like Rs 476 Cr in operating cash flow [E33] are entirely overwhelmed by a ballooning working capital requirement, with working capital days expanding dramatically from 80.1 days to 142 days [E59]. Furthermore, borrowings have escalated to Rs 1,570 Cr up from Rs 1,227 Cr a year earlier [E37], and promoter holdings have diluted from 74.20% to 71.80% [E39]. While institutional accumulation occurred [E40, E41, E42] and sector tailwinds exist [E69, E71], the current price demands an unrealistic 25.7% earnings growth according to the reverse DCF [E45], leaving a staggering -73.3% margin of safety against the intrinsic DCF value of Rs 598 [E43, E44].
